prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1151; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left-turn lane when the vehicle turned across the path of Driver 2, and the front of Driver 1's vehicle struck the side of Driver 2's vehicle at the intersection in Pearland, Texas. Driver 1 reported neck pain at the scene and was evaluated by emergency medical personnel. The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of this impact. Driver 1 and Driver 2 both stated that a Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle at the time, and the Passenger's presence was confirmed by both drivers. No independent witnesses were located at the scene. Scene photographs confirm the positions of both vehicles and several areas of damage, and the visible damage is largely in line with the described collision. Neither driver reported, and the responding officer did not observe, any prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 2 is the named policyholder on the insurance policy for the vehicle and resides in the same household as Driver 1. Citations were not issued at the scene pending further review of the collision.
